findings.issue_text: Credential-sync requests lack a secret or authorization header, forcing the token-minting endpoint to be unauthenticated and allowing arbitrary user IDs and app slugs to obtain OAuth access tokens
Credentials are matched only by userId and appId, so users with multiple accounts for one integration can have an arbitrary credential overwritten
The non-atomic findFirst-then-create sequence allows concurrent webhook deliveries to create duplicate credentials for the same user and app
Using z.string().toString() as computed schema keys produces the literal key "[object Object]", causing key collisions and stripping actual expiry and token fields

The relaxed sync schema is selected from global environment state even when team credentials fall back to the provider, stripping valid provider response fields and potentially replacing the refresh token with the literal "refresh_token"
Google Calendar stores the entire {success, data} parse result as the credential key, corrupting credentials after refresh even when credential sharing is disabled
Google Calendar treats the native Response returned in sync mode as a Gaxios response and reads res.data, leaving the token undefined and causing refresh to crash
HubSpot casts the native Response returned in sync mode directly to HubspotToken without parsing the body, leaving access-token and expiry fields undefined
Zoho Bigin treats the native Response returned in sync mode as an Axios response and dereferences tokenInfo.data, causing a runtime exception
Zoho Bigin passes credentialId as calcomUserId, which can retrieve credentials for the wrong user or no user when credential and user IDs differ
Zoho CRM treats the native Response returned in sync mode as an Axios response and accesses zohoCrmTokenInfo.data, causing token refresh to fail at runtime
Salesforce refreshes and persists a token on every service construction even when the access token is valid, increasing endpoint traffic and risking provider rate limits

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Credential-sync requests lack a secret or authorization header, forcing the token-minting endpoint to be unauthenticated and allowing arbitrary user IDs and app slugs to obtain OAuth access tokens

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the refreshOAuthTokens function in packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, it makes a POST request to the sync endpoint with only calcomUserId and appSlug in the body. There is no Authorization header, no webhook secret, or any authentication mechanism added to this outgoing request. This means the external credential sync endpoint would need to be either unauthenticated or rely on some other mechanism not shown in this code. The finding correctly identifies that the outgoing requests to fetch tokens lack authentication headers, which could be a security concern if the endpoint is expected to mint OAuth tokens.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Credentials are matched only by userId and appId, so users with multiple accounts for one integration can have an arbitrary credential overwritten

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the webhook handler in apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts, the code finds credentials using `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId: reqBody.userId, appId: appMetadata.slug } })`. If a user has multiple credentials for the same app (e.g., multiple Google Calendar accounts), this query will return only the first one found, and then update that specific credential. The finding is correct that this could overwrite an arbitrary credential when multiple exist for the same user/app combination. However, looking at the typical use case described in the comments (self-hosters implementing Cal.com into their applications), this appears to be designed for syncing a single credential per app per user from an external system. The behavior is deterministic (always updates the first found), but could indeed cause issues if users legitimately have multiple accounts for one integration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The non-atomic findFirst-then-create sequence allows concurrent webhook deliveries to create duplicate credentials for the same user and app

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the webhook handler in apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts, lines 56-75 show a findFirst query followed by either an update or create operation. This is indeed a non-atomic operation - if two concurrent webhook requests arrive for the same userId and appId, both could execute findFirst before either executes create, resulting in duplicate credentials being created. This is a real race condition bug in the code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: HubSpot casts the native Response returned in sync mode directly to HubspotToken without parsing the body, leaving access-token and expiry fields undefined

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the HubSpot CalendarService.ts diff, the refreshOAuthTokens function wraps the hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken call. In the 'else' branch of refreshOAuthTokens (when credential sync is disabled), it returns `await refreshFunction()` which would return the HubspotToken from the SDK. However, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, it returns a raw fetch Response object. The code then assigns this directly to `hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken` without parsing the response body. This is a real bug - in sync mode, the Response object would be assigned to hubspotRefreshToken, and accessing properties like access_token would be undefined since Response doesn't have those properties directly.
